artboards.title: Lisbon — the port as a place
At sea — the chart is the screen

annotations.text:
TODAY

One column, top to bottom. Eight equal tabs treat Market and Profile as the same kind of thing. Nothing tells you where you are — only which document you are reading.

THE PORT IS A PLACE

You are standing on a quay, not reading a page. Facilities are doors, and each door carries the one live fact that decides whether you go in.

Tap a door — it opens OVER the harbour, so you never lose where you are. The eight tabs collapse to three things that follow you: FLEET, CHART, LOG.

THE MARKET

%NBR was a sixth column that fell off the right edge of a 390px phone — the one number the game turns on, invisible. It is a bar now, first and full width.

And the two things that cost a real voyage: WHERE it sells dearer (the bookkeeper), and what a PARCEL actually costs — 133 a tun, not the 131 on the label.

AT SEA

While she is sailing the chart IS the screen, not a tab you visit.

Standing orders read as a numbered sentence, and a mis-ordered pair says so BEFORE it runs — the queue currently accepts 'sail home' ahead of 'sell' in silence, which is a guaranteed loss you only find in the ledger.
